title: God tests for benefit
english: There God set ordinances and judgments for him, and there he was testing him (Exodus 15:25). God tests for our benefit. For he is untested by evils. But he tests for this reason: so that if they obey him, they may obtain good things and be delivered from evils.
orientation: Origen begins his commentary on Exodus 15:25, explaining why God tested Israel at the place where he gave them ordinances and judgments.

title: Idol versus likeness; bowing versus serving
english: "You shall not make for yourself an idol" (Exodus 20:4). An idol is one thing, and a likeness is another. For it is a likeness if you make a likeness of a fish or a four-footed animal or a beast, whether by craftsmanship or by painting. But an idol is whatever the soul forms as an image and makes from things that do not exist in an original way—for example, a mixed creature from a human and a horse.
"Whatever is in heaven above, and whatever is on the earth below, and whatever is in the waters under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you serve them" (Exodus 20:5).

Bowing down is one thing, and serving is another. For the one who serves these things from the whole soul does not only bow down but also serves. But the one who plays the hypocrite and acts for the sake of custom does not serve, yet he does bow down. You will find such people in Numbers, gratifying women and bowing down to idols.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Exodus 20:4-5, explaining the difference between an idol and a likeness, and between bowing down and serving.

title: The high priest's protective care before and behind
english: It is fitting that the high priest carry protective care both in front and behind, like a shield, so that no hostile counsel of the evil spirits may wound the rational soul, disturb the soundness of its judgments, and by the admixture of evil make its clarity and truth depart.
orientation: Origen is explaining the high priest's front and back covering as complete protective care against hostile spiritual powers.

title: Why God kept Moses forty days
english: And the Lord spoke to Moses (Exodus 31:1). The all-wise God held Moses for whole forty days to give the law, although he was fully able to give the law in three days. But he did this so that the time of Moses' absence might expose the hidden impiety in the depth of the Jews' hearts.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Exodus 31:1, explaining why God kept Moses on the mountain for forty days before giving the law.
